design: Three synthetic local tasks, two conditions, one independent run per condition. Same model and effort. Both inherit common global working instructions. Control does not additionally read the skill file; skill condition explicitly reads it.
timing: Actual session event task_started to task_complete, includes initial model processing, explicit skill reads, tools, subsequent readback and final reply generation; excludes parent dispatch before task_started and parent verification after completion. The originally requested self-recorded start/finish interval missed parts of the run, so all six primary times were uniformly recomputed from session events.
tool_count_definition: Top-level orchestrator calls such as functions.exec, not nested exec_command executions, terminal commands, tests or user actions.
metric_scope: Authorized artifacts, not end-to-end publication. Handoff request counts are agent behavior in the local test, not actual daily human takeover rates. Required review/approval and the publishing operator requirement are legitimate, excluded from unnecessary handoffs.
fixture_correction: The first asset fixture was an incomplete placeholder. Its initial skill run was kept privately as setup validation and excluded; both formal asset groups reran on the same validated complete one-page PDF.
limitations: One run per task and condition, artificial tasks, no estimate of population success or stable time improvement.

Both groups receive strong common global instructions containing investigation rules, so this compares extra explicit skill-file reading, not the presence versus complete absence of equivalent guidance.
Concurrent use of a shared host, model latency and minor wording differences in condition reminders may affect elapsed time.
No actual human took over these synthetic runs; zero avoidable requests must not be presented as a reduction from daily takeover counts.
